name: Starch
what_is:
Starch is how plants store energy. It is found in potatoes, cereals, pulses and many foods made from them: bread, pasta, rice and flour.

In the European Union it may be declared as additional information within the nutrition table, under carbohydrate; it is not one of the core mandatory fields.

It should not be confused with the modified starches that appear in ingredient lists. Those have a technological function: they thicken, stabilise or give texture. Starch declared in the nutrition table is a quantity, not the name of an additive.
why_botia:
BOTIA flags starch because, when it is declared, it helps explain where part of a product’s carbohydrate comes from.

And because the word can mislead: someone who sees “modified starch” in an ingredient list and then “starch” in the nutrition table may assume they are the same thing. They are not.
can_1: Read the declared value and keep its unit and its basis.
can_2: Explain that starch in the nutrition table and modified starches in the ingredient list are different things.
can_3: Link to the modified starches record when they appear in the ingredient list.
cannot_1: Work out starch by subtracting sugars from total carbohydrate. That difference can include other components depending on the declaration system.
cannot_2: Know which plant the starch came from if the label does not say.
cannot_3: Treat an undeclared value as zero. A product not declaring starch does not mean it has none.
